routes.description: Establish generic theism through libertarian agency and cosmic causation, then use resurrection evidence to identify the inferred God with Christian theism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its theistic premises warrant a personal transcendent cause and the historical evidence warrants divine resurrection as the specifically Christian identification.

motionBridge.description: Generic theism and divine resurrection must jointly warrant the existence of the Christian God.

centralBridges.description: Human deliberation must support libertarian freedom, and that freedom must be better explained by a divine mind than by naturalistic determinism.
The universe must have begun from a cause whose relation to all physical reality warrants timeless, spaceless, immaterial, powerful agency.
The historical facts concerning Jesus must make divine resurrection the warranted explanation after relevant background evidence is considered.
Limited divine manifestation and competing religious claims must remain compatible with God's purposes and Christianity's distinctive evidential case.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Philosophical and historical inquiry must be admissible for questions that scientific instruments cannot directly detect.
The Christian hypothesis must expose identifiable conceptual or historical conditions under which it would be undermined.

routes.description: Withhold belief unless the offered methods and evidence discriminate Christian theism from natural, unknown, and rival religious explanations.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the affirmative evidence does not reliably establish its crucial premises or uniquely connect generic causes, experiences, and testimony to the Christian God.

motionBridge.description: The Christian conclusion must remain unwarranted when its evidence does not reliably discriminate it from competing explanations.

centralBridges.description: The methods used for theism must demonstrate enough reliability to justify their conclusions rather than merely accommodate them.
Libertarian freedom must be independently supported and coherent with an omniscient creator before it can serve as evidence for God.
A cause of the universe must not be identified as a personal transcendent deity without justified intermediate inferences.
Resurrection claims must rest on confirmable historical data and outperform ordinary, unknown, and rival explanations.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Reasonable nonbelief and divided revelation must be assessed against the expected communication of a truth-seeking Christian God.
Evidence shared by incompatible religions must acquire a warranted bridge to specifically Christian theism.

sectionSelections.title: Libertarian agency and rational belief
sectionSelections.rationale: This issue bears on an independent argument for God and on whether evidence-responsive reasoning requires the ability to choose otherwise.

proSelections.proposition: Libertarian human freedom exists, cannot be accommodated by naturalistic determinism, and is therefore best explained by God's existence.
A deterministic system may produce true outputs, but rational belief requires deliberative selection among reasons and therefore depends on libertarian freedom.

conSelections.proposition: Libertarian freedom is unsupported and conflicts with a creator who knowingly selects a complete universe and whose plan and prophecies fix how events unfold.
Determinism does not prevent a decision-making agent from revising beliefs in response to new information, so rational change does not require libertarian choice.

sectionSelections.title: Cosmic causation and the nature of the cause
sectionSelections.rationale: The causal argument is a principal route to generic theism, and its burden depends on the transition from a cosmic beginning to a personal transcendent cause.

proSelections.proposition: Because everything that begins has a cause and the universe began, its best explanation is a timeless, spaceless, immaterial, powerful mind.
The cause of all contiguous physical reality must transcend space, time, and matter, and state-to-event causation further supports an agent with libertarian freedom.

conSelections.proposition: The Kalam establishes at most that the universe had a cause, while identifying that cause as a transcendent personal God requires unsupported additional assertions.
Even granting that the universe has a cause or explanation, the Kalam argument supplies no justified knowledge about what that cause is.

sectionSelections.title: Resurrection evidence and historical inference
sectionSelections.rationale: This issue supplies the proposed bridge from generic theism to Christian identity and tests whether historical testimony can warrant divine resurrection.

proSelections.proposition: Prior reason to accept God and Jesus's claimed divine mission raises the antecedent plausibility of God resurrecting Jesus.
Jesus's crucifixion, reported post-death appearances, and the disciples' costly commitment make divine resurrection the best historical explanation.

conSelections.proposition: Historical conclusions require comparative background support and may remain uncertain, while an unrestricted divine explanation lacks discriminatory explanatory force.
The resurrection's proposed minimal facts are not independently confirmable, and scholarly agreement or assessments cannot substitute for the underlying historical data.

sectionSelections.title: Divine hiddenness, revelation, and Christian specificity
sectionSelections.rationale: Reasonable nonbelief and competing revelations directly affect whether the observed world fits the Christian God's aims and whether the cumulative case identifies Christianity uniquely.

proSelections.proposition: General theistic arguments can legitimately support God before resurrection evidence identifies that deity as the Christian God.
Divine hiddenness is weakened because substantial evidence for God already exists and God seeks freely chosen trust and loyalty rather than mere compelled intellectual assent.

conSelections.proposition: A God who wants people to know him should generate observable expectations, so pervasive reasonable nonbelief is substantial disconfirming evidence for that God model.
Competing and internally divided revelations undermine Christianity because believers identify errors in rival traditions without applying the same skepticism to their own.

sectionSelections.title: Method reliability and evidential warrant
sectionSelections.rationale: The governing evidential method determines whether philosophical and historical considerations can warrant theism and whether revisability alone supplies justification.

proSelections.proposition: Scientific methods are not the only reliable tools of inquiry; philosophy and history can investigate questions outside science's proper detection range.

conSelections.proposition: No demonstrated methodology reliably supports the existence of any god, whereas scientific methods earn confidence through consistently reliable results.
The central disagreement is not willingness to change one's mind but whether the evidence originally used to justify Christian belief is sufficiently reliable.
